s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratosis and hyperpigmentation
salient_findings: Hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales
key_facts: Lesions did not improve with topical corticosteroids
Symmetrical distribution over the dorsum of both feet and around the knees
Negative hepatitis C and B serologies
Normal levels of aspartate and alanine aminotransferases
Plasma zinc at the lower end of normal

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and peripheral rim of erythema

shortlist.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic plaques with hyperkeratosis and hyperpigmentation

shortlist.label: Dermatophytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic plaques with hyperkeratosis and peripheral rim of erythema

shortlist.label: Hypothyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone and dry skin

raw.rationale: The presence of well-defined hyperpigmented, hyperkeratotic plaques with thick adherent scales and a peripheral rim of erythema, along with the symmetrical distribution over the dorsum of both feet and around the knees, are characteristic of psoriasis. The lack of response to topical corticosteroids also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pityriasis rubra pilaris
rejected.why: Typically presents with orange-red scaling plaques and palmoplantar keratoderma, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Usually presents with flat-topped, violaceous papules and oral mucosal involvement, which are not described in the case

rejected.label: Dermatophytosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with annular, scaly plaques and is usually responsive to antifungal treatment, which is not mentioned

rejected.label: Hypothyroidism
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated thyroid-stimulating hormone, the skin findings are not typical of hypothyroidism, which usually presents with dry skin, cold intolerance, and hair loss
